answer.rationale: The write-path latency degradation began ~90 minutes ago, roughly aligning with a release pushed 2 hours prior, making rollback the most plausible high-leverage single intervention. memory_b1 directly documents a prior rollback resolving a similar checkout error spike cleanly, so it's the most relevant record to verify before committing scarce intervention capacity. Given settlement traffic is at daily peak and writes are heavy, I flag downstream value risk: a rollback must be executed as a guarded, monitored action rather than a broad forced cutover, to avoid dropping or corrupting in-flight settlement writes. I'm not treating the release as confirmed root cause—only correlated in time—so I preserve uncertainty and would monitor p99 and write-success metrics immediately post-rollback, ready to pivot to regional_failover or circuit_breaker if rollback doesn't quickly arrest the latency climb.
